notes: Each run starts in a fresh clone of this repository. `setup` says what to place under profile/ and datasets/ before the prompt is sent; `files` lists the fixtures it draws on, relative to the skill directory. files/data/exercises.json is the offline self-test fixture, laid out where assets/datasets.json's data_file expects it, so no clone is needed. Assertions are graded against the transcript and the files left behind.

evals.name: plain-plan-from-fixtures
evals.expected_output: Reads the profile and the latest program file, re-confirms the five program answers in one pre-filled batch (keeping all is one choice), notes no rules.md is present, uses the local dataset cache, runs scripts/generate.py --brief, chooses a week from the brief and hands it back with --selection, shows the planned-versus-allocated table, the week and every warning plus the two exact paths before writing, then writes profile/plans/plan-<today>.json and plan-<today>.md and nothing else.
assertions: The transcript re-confirms goal, days per week, session length, split and deload with their saved values before generating
The transcript shows a per-muscle planned-versus-allocated table and the day-by-day week before any plan file is written
The transcript names both output paths under profile/plans/ before writing them
profile/plans/ contains exactly one .json and one .md with the same date stem, and the .json validates against skills/generation/assets/schema/plan.schema.json
The plan's per-muscle targets equal the program file's volume.per_muscle_weekly_sets exactly (no recomputation)
profile/profile.json and profile/programs/program-2026-08-06.json are byte-identical to the fixtures, and no profile/rules.md was created
The transcript shows scripts/generate.py invoked twice — once with --brief, once with --selection plus --write and --write-md; the week was chosen from the brief, not composed by hand

evals.name: program-without-volume-block
evals.prompt: give me a plan for this cycle
evals.expected_output: Notices volume is null in the latest program file, refuses to estimate targets, and either runs the onboarding volume step (python skills/onboarding/scripts/volume.py --profile profile/profile.json --write profile/programs/program-2026-08-06.json) or hands that exact command back — then continues only once the block exists. Under no circumstances does it invent per-muscle set targets.
assertions: The transcript states that the program file has no volume block before doing anything else with the dataset
The transcript contains the volume.py command with --profile and --write pointing at the real files, either run or handed back
No plan file is written while volume is still null
If a plan was written, the program file now has a non-null volume block that volume.py produced (integer per_muscle_weekly_sets summing to weekly_sets_allocated) and the plan targets equal it
No per-muscle set numbers appear in the transcript that did not come from volume.py output

evals.name: one-off-exclusion-no-squats
evals.prompt: same program as last time but no squats this cycle, my knee's grumpy
evals.expected_output: Keeps the saved program answers, treats 'no squats' as a one-off rules file passed with --rules for this run (not a hand-edit of the output and not a write to profile/rules.md), regenerates, shows the table/week/warnings/paths, writes the plan pair, and offers a paste-ready rules.md snippet in case the exclusion should stick.
assertions: No exercise in the written plan has 'squat' in its name
profile/rules.md does not exist after the run (the skill never writes it)
The transcript shows the exclusion was applied through a rules file passed to the generator, not by editing the generated week
The transcript offers a paste-ready rules.md snippet containing the squat exclusion, as Markdown bullets under an '## Exclude exercises' heading rather than JSON
The plan's per-muscle targets still equal the program file's volume.per_muscle_weekly_sets; any shortfall from dropping squats appears in the plan's warnings and in the transcript
profile/plans/ contains exactly one .json and one .md
